oneOf.description: Astrid runs it. Nothing to set up.
The account's own agent asks for work.
The account's own agent is told about work.

AgentRow.description: One agent, and the ways it may be set to run.

email.description: The address comments and assignments show for it, when the server said.

id.description: The mailbox — the local part of the agent's address, and what a mode write names.

locked.description: Whether it has no server-side executor and so can only be polled or switched off.

mode.description: How it runs now, as the server resolved it.

modes.description: The modes a control may offer for it. Never a mode the server would refuse.

name.description: What to call it on screen.

AssigneeOption.description: One row of the picker. `user_id: None` is the unassigned choice.

initials.description: Avatar fallback. Empty for the unassigned row, which has its own glyph.

name.description:
What to show where a name goes, or `None` for the unassigned row — which the shell names
from its resources rather than being handed a word.

user.description:
The person's record as the pools hold it, for a shell that draws its own avatar from a
user (the Apple apps). `None` for the unassigned row.

Attachment.description: A legacy file attachment. Superseded by [`SecureFile`]; still returned on older tasks.

Block.description: One block of a rendered text, top to bottom.

oneOf.description:
A fenced or indented code block. Drawn monospace, and it scrolls sideways rather than
widening whatever it is in (the web's `.prose pre`).

start.description: The first number of an ordered list. `1` for a bulleted one.

oneOf.description:
A table whose body cells all lead with a rating (`++`, `~`, `🔴`): a trade-off grid, drawn
with each rated cell on its colour (astrid-web AWTD-1524; this block, AWTD-1626). Which
tables are grids is [`crate::decisions::is_tradeoff_grid`], on each cell's source text as
the web reads it.

The shell numbers rows from 1 and letters criteria A, B, C by position
([`crate::decisions::column_letter`]); neither is in the block.

alignments.description: One per column, the option column first: `left`, `center`, `right` or `none`.

header.description: The option column's heading, then one per criterion.

key.description: The label keys the grid's key shows, worst to best: each rating used, once.

virtualKey.description: Set for the channels that belong to a virtual list rather than a stored one.

authorId.description: Absent on the messages the server authors itself.

type.description: The same TEXT/MARKDOWN/ATTACHMENT enum comments use.

authorId.description: Absent on system comments, which the server authors itself.

clientRequestId.description: The server echoes the `temp_<uuid>` idempotency key back. Offline dedup depends on it.

id.description:
Mutable because an offline comment is created with a `temp_` id and keeps its identity when
the server's id arrives.

remoteAuthorLogin.description:
The GitHub login of a commenter with no Astrid account (AWTD-1283). Set only when
`author_id` and `author` are both absent, and it makes the comment a person's, not the
server's — see [`Comment::is_system`].

remoteNodeId.description:
The GitHub comment this one mirrors, on a GitHub Projects deployment (AWTD-1283).
Informational only.

authorId.description:
The author's id, photo and initials, for the face beside the bubble (iOS's comment thread,
AATD-53).

authorIsAgent.description: Whether an AI agent wrote it — a reply that also ends that agent's "is thinking..." (AATD-53).

authorName.description: Who wrote it, or `None` for one the server authored.

blocks.description:
The text as the web draws it — through the same markdown a description gets, so a
mention is a pill and `**bold**` is bold (task 3271a0c5). Empty when there is no text.

indentRight.description:
Which side a reply is set in from: the parent author's, as the web does it — replies to
my comment step in from the right, replies to yours from the left.

isMine.description:
Which side of the thread it sits on.

A chat transcript is unreadable without it: every bubble on the same side is one voice, and
a thread drawn all on one side says the other person never replied.

isPending.description: Still in the Outbox. Not an error — the same meaning it has in a chat transcript.

isReply.description:
Drawn nested under its parent. False for a reply whose parent is not in the thread, which
is then an ordinary comment rather than an indent under nothing.

isSystem.description: Nobody wrote it — the server did. Drawn as a centred note rather than as either voice.

parentId.description: The comment this one answers, when it answers one (task 97c817dd).

showsText.description: Whether to draw a text bubble at all.

CountForm.description:
What a number in a message is counting — and so which of CLDR's two sets of rules applies.

They are genuinely different rules, not two uses of one: English's *cardinal* 3 is `other`
("3 weeks") while its *ordinal* 3 is `few` ("3rd"). Nothing can pick the right form without
being told which question is being asked, and the arm that chose the key already knows.

oneOf.description: Which one in order: "the 3rd Tuesday", "on the 21st".

CredentialRow.description: One service the account can hold a key for.

configured.description: Whether a key is stored. Never the key: the server does not answer with one.

error.description: What went wrong the last time it was tested, when the server kept a reason.

isValid.description:
Whether the stored key worked the last time it was tested.

Three states, not two. `None` is **never tested**, which is not "broken": a key saved a
minute ago and a key the provider has revoked are different rows, and a screen that drew
both as a red cross would send somebody to re-paste a key that is fine.

keyPreview.description:
Enough of the stored key to tell which one it is, exactly as the server masked it —
`first4***last4`, or `***` for a key of eight characters or fewer, or the first twenty
characters of an OpenClaw gateway URL. `None` when no key is stored.

This is a preview, never the key. The masking is the server's
(`app/api/v1/users/me/ai-credentials/route.ts`, `getKeyPreview`) and is not recomputed
here: a client that re-masked would be a client that could disagree with the screen
somebody pasted the key into.

lastTested.description: When it was last tested, as the server timestamped it.

name.description: What to call it on screen.

serviceId.description: What the API calls it, and what a save or a delete has to send back.

CustomRepeatingPattern.description:
The custom repeat pattern, kept as loose as it is on the wire.

Every field is optional because the shape depends on `unit` and the server has never validated
the combination. Interpretation lives in [`crate::repeating`] and nowhere else.

key.description:
The string-catalog key for its label, or `None` when the value is its own label — an
hour, which only the reader's clock can spell.

value.description:
What choosing this stores on the list. `None` is a real choice, not an absence: no
priority is `"0"`, but all-day is the *lack* of a time.

DeleteTaskMode.description:
`list.supports.deleteTask`. A GitHub board takes the item off the project and leaves the issue.
A value this build does not know reads as the classic one.

Failure.description:
Why a command did not work.

One shape for every failure — a kind, a message, and the two optional details that some kinds
carry — rather than a tagged union whose payload differs per case. The shell reads this in C#,
where a shape that changes per variant is a `switch` over `JsonElement` at every call site.

code.description:
A machine-readable reason within the kind, when there is one — `WAITING_NEEDS_CONDITION`
(a move into Waiting with no date and no task to wait on: show the picker). The server's
own `code`, when a refusal carried one. Absent otherwise; a shell that does not know a code
treats the failure by its kind.

message.description: For a person to read, and for a log. Never the thing to branch on.

status.description: The HTTP status, when the server gave one.

FailureKind.description: What kind of failure it was. The part the shell branches on.

oneOf.description: The shell sent something this build cannot read.
The session is gone. Sign in again — retrying will not help.
The server considered it and said no.

It did not reach the server. **Not necessarily a failure**: a write is already journalled
and will go when the network does. The shell shows this as "offline", not as an error.
The thing being acted on is not here.
The cache could not be read or written.

localPath.description:
Where its bytes are on this machine, when they are already here.

`None` is not an error — it means "not fetched yet", and the chip is what a screen draws
until they are. Filled in by [`with_local_paths`] rather than by [`rows`], which stays a
pure function of the comments.

rendersInline.description: Whether it is drawn in the comment or offered as a chip to open.

FilterGroup.description: One filter: the field it writes, and the choices for it.

field.description: The field on the list, as the API spells it — `filterPriority`, `sortBy`, and so on.

FilterPick.description: One choice, and whether the list is set to it.

field.description:
The field this choice writes. Carried on the pick as well as the group because a shell
draws picks one at a time, and a radio button that does not know which group it is in is a
radio button that clears the wrong one.

value.description: The value to write back, exactly as [`crate::filters`] matches it.

GithubApp.description: What a GitHub App panel needs in one answer.

active.description:
Whether at least one installation is actually honoured — installed, and not suspended.
The question "will anything work", which `installed` alone does not answer.

installations.description: Every installation, oldest access first, as the server ordered them.

installed.description: Whether the App is installed anywhere at all.

GridCell.description: One criterion's cell in a trade-off grid.

inlines.description:
The reason, without its rating. A cell that is only a rating shows the token, so it still
reads where colour does not.

rating.description:
The rating's label key (`veryPoor`, `poor`, `mixed`, `good`, `veryGood`), or `None` for an
empty cell. The key, not the token: `-` and `🔴` are drawn alike.

GridRow.description: One option of a trade-off grid.

name.description: The option, without the marker its writer put in front (`A. Lisbon` → `Lisbon`).

link.description:
Where the run goes when clicked, when it goes anywhere: an absolute `http`, `https` or
`mailto` address.

oneOf.description: One of Astrid's pills: a person, a list or a task, by id.

InstallationRow.description: One installation of the GitHub App, as the server summarises it.

accountLogin.description: The user or organisation it is installed on.

accountType.description:
`User` or `Organization`, when the server said. Absent is not an error: an older
deployment did not record it.

id.description:
GitHub's installation id. A number on the wire; kept as text because it is only ever an
identifier here, and a client that rounded it would address the wrong installation.

repositorySelection.description: `all` or `selected` — whether the App can see every repository or a chosen few.

suspended.description: Suspended on GitHub: the row exists and nothing it grants works.

ListAgentConfig.description:
`{ enabledTypes, defaultAgentId, allowMemberAssignment }` — the shape the server stores and,
since 2026-08-29, emits as `aiAgentConfig` beside the plain `aiAgentsEnabled` array. It carries
the default agent the array cannot express.

allowMemberAssignment.description:
Whether a member, rather than only an admin, may assign a task to an agent on this list.

Carried so the wire round trip loses nothing; nothing in the core reads it yet, and gating
on it is a dispatch decision rather than a model one. `Option` rather than `bool` because
absent and `false` are different answers, and defaulting the key in would invent it on a
surface that never sent it.

ListDefaultPicks.description: Every picker the defaults editor draws.

ListItem.description: One item of a list: its own blocks, and a checkbox if it is a task-list item.

checked.description: `Some` for a `- [ ]` / `- [x]` item; `None` for an ordinary one.

ListMember.description: Someone's membership of a list. Presence IS membership; the role only refines what it allows.

id.description:
Absent in the embedded member arrays some responses return (creating a task, for one), and
the user id stands in — see [`ListMember::identity`].

ListPick.description: One list as the picker draws it.

ListPicks.description: What the editor shows for one task and one search.

createName.description: The name to offer creating, when what was typed is not a list yet.

options.description: The lists it could be added to that match the search.

selected.description: The lists the task is in, in the task's own order.

ListRemote.description:
`list.remote`: which GitHub Project a GitHub-backed list mirrors (web
`lib/backends/list-wire.ts`).

The counterpart of [`super::task::TaskRemote`] one level up, and a simpler shape: web fills all
three keys or sends `null` for the whole object, never a partial one — `null` for a classic
list, for an iteration list, which is a tag rather than a bound board, and for a board whose
GitHub installation row has gone. They are still `#[serde(default)]`, for the same reason every
field in this module is: a thinner payload from a server this build does not know must not fail
the whole list.

number.description: The project's number in that account, which is how GitHub itself names it.

owner.description: The GitHub account the project belongs to: an organisation's login, or a person's.

ListSupports.description:
`list.supports` on the wire: what a list's backend can do that a client would otherwise have
to guess. Every key is at its classic value when absent, and the web adds a key as each
capability lands (`lib/backends/supports.ts`) — so a key this build does not know is ignored
rather than refused.

deleteTask.description: What deleting a task does here.

dueDate.description: A due date can be set. False on a GitHub board with no date field mapped.

fields.description: Tasks here can carry the project's own field values (web AWTD-1208).

membership.description: Members and invitations are managed in Astrid. On a GitHub board the roster is GitHub's.

multipleAssignees.description: A task here may hold several assignees (`assigneeIds`). Classic lists keep at most one.

priority.description: Priority can be set. False on a GitHub board with no Priority field mapped.

privateTasks.description: `isPrivate` means something here. A GitHub board's tasks are as visible as its project.

repeatMode.description: How a repeating task here advances when it is completed (web AWTD-1118, spec §10).

ListToggle.description: One row of the Apple pickers: a list, and whether the task is in it.

ListToggles.description: What the Apple pickers show (AITD-461, `docs/CONTRACTS.md` D50 — iOS's `InlineListsPicker`).

options.description: Every list it can be filed in that matches the search, selected ones included.

selected.description: The lists the task is in, as chips, in the order below.

MessageRow.description: One message, as the shell draws it.

authorName.description: Who said it, or `None` when the server did.

blocks.description:
What the message says, as blocks a screen can draw — the same projection a comment and a
description get (task 5f3453e2).

Web has always drawn chat through `renderMarkdownWithLinks`; Windows drew `content` into a
text block, so a task id in a conversation could only be retyped, and `**bold**` arrived
with its asterisks. `content` stays for whoever wants the text as written — a reply
preview, an accessibility name, a copy.

initials.description: Avatar fallback. Empty for a message nobody said.

isMine.description: Whether the signed-in account wrote it. Which side the bubble sits on.

isPending.description: Still in the Outbox. Not an error — see the module note.

isSystem.description: Written by the server rather than by a person.

actorId.description: Who caused it. Never the reader — nobody is told what they just did.

kind.description:
`assigned` | `mentioned` | `replied` | `commented` | `status_changed` | `completed`, and
whatever a newer server adds — kept as text so an unknown kind still draws.

task.description: The task it is about, as the route summarises it. Absent when the task is gone.

NotificationTask.description: What the inbox knows about a task without opening it.

Priority.description:
How urgent, 0-3.

**Decoded leniently.** The server's schema puts no cap on `priority`, and two production tasks
were observed carrying `4`. Swift's default enum decode threw on those, which failed the decode
of the WHOLE tasks array and silently broke sync for that account. An unknown value reads as
[`Priority::None`] so the task stays usable.

customStates.description:
The board's own columns, and renames of the three defaults.

Free-form JSON on the wire, and read rather than typed: an entry a newer web writes must not
stop a board drawing. [`crate::board::parse_custom_states`] is the only place that reads it.

key.description:
The prefix this project's task identifiers carry — `AWTD` in `AWTD-1007`.

Unique across astrid.cc, and `None` for a project made before identifiers existed. The
server is the only minter; this is read so a client knows which keys the reader can see,
which is what decides whether `AWTD-1007` in a comment becomes a link
([`crate::identifier::find_links`], task 5f3453e2).

id.description: Omitted by the embedded member arrays, like [`super::list::ListMember`].

RecentlyCompletedWindow.description:
How far back "Recently completed" reaches for one list.

Mirrors `astrid-web/lib/recently-completed-window.ts`, discriminated by `kind`. The same
setting drives the list view's default completion filter and the board's Done column, so the
two views can never disagree. `None` on the list means the legacy 24-hour default.

ReminderPick.description: One choice, and the instant it means.

reminderTime.description: The instant to store, or `None` for "no reminder".

RepeatFromMode.description: Whether the next occurrence is measured from the due date or from when it was actually done.

RepeatMode.description:
`list.supports.repeatMode`. On a GitHub board the completed issue stays closed as history and
the next occurrence is a NEW task the server makes, so a client sends the completion and does
not roll the row forward itself. A value this build does not know reads as the classic one:
rolling forward is recoverable, a series silently dropped is not.

RepeatPreset.description: One choice in the repeat picker.

value.description: The value to write back, exactly as the wire spells it: `never`, `daily`, …, `custom`.

Response.description:
What a command answered.

`value` is deliberately untyped, and that is a fact the wire schema has to state rather than
paper over: the payload differs per command, and what IS describable — the row and detail
projections a shell decodes it into — is named in the schema on its own (task 9ef7edb4).

Sections.description: The sidebar's sections, in the order they are drawn down the side.

favorites.description: Favourites, in the order the user arranged them. The web's "Saved Filters" section.

lists.description: Everything else that can hold a task, by name.

myTasks.description:
My Tasks: what you are holding, wherever it lives. Above the favourites, because it is the
view the app opens on rather than one of the lists. `None` when the caller did not ask for
it — it is synthesised and has no row on the server, so only the caller can say.

SecureFile.description:
A file held by the server's secure-file store. The wire names differ from the field names, and
those aliases are the whole reason this type is hand-mapped.

SummaryPart.description: One fragment of the sentence: a key, plus whatever it interpolates.

count.description: The number the key's plural form and its `{0}` refer to, when it has one.

form.description:
What [`Self::count`] is counting, and so which of CLDR's two sets of rules picks its form
(task 3564db06). Present exactly when there is a count.

The arm that chose the key already knows whether its number is a quantity or a position,
and this is that knowledge crossing the boundary instead of being re-derived. Without it a
shell has to keep a list of which keys are ordinals and an `st`/`nd`/`rd`/`th` helper to
serve them — which is English's rule, applied in every language.

key.description: A resource key. Never a word.

values.description:
Names the key interpolates — weekdays as the wire spells them, so the shell translates
them from its own table rather than being handed English.

assigneeIds.description:
Everyone assigned, as the server sent it (web AWTD-1190). Only a list whose backend
supports several assignees ever holds more than one. Never read this directly:
[`Task::all_assignee_ids`] is the list a client shows, because `assignee_id` is written on
its own — by an older client, or by an optimistic reassignment here — and stays the truth
about who is first.

blockedBy.description:
The tasks this one is waiting on, by id, and the tasks waiting on it.

`GET /api/v1/tasks/:id` adds both beside `listIds`, and the wire contract
(`astrid-web/lib/api-contracts/v1-ios-shapes.ts`, `V1TaskBlockerIds`) makes them
**optional** so the server and each client ship independently: a deployment older than the
feature simply does not send them, which reads here as "nothing known", never as "nothing".

Ids only. The titles a chip draws come from `GET /api/v1/tasks/:id/blockers`, because a
blocker the reader cannot see has an id and nothing else — and the difference between that
and a blocker that merely has not synced yet is the one thing the row must not get wrong.
Needs no cache migration: the store keeps each model's whole JSON and lifts out only the
columns something queries.

closedReason.description:
Why the task was closed, when it was closed as anything but done: `canceled` |
`duplicate` | `not_planned` (web task 11042ae3). The web keeps `completed` true beside it,
so every view that reads the flag keeps working; only the rendering and the repeat rollover
differ. Kept as text rather than an enum so a reason this build has never heard of cannot
make the whole task unreadable.

completedAt.description: The real completion time, which sync may backdate.

creatorId.description:
The MCP API returns the creator object without the id field, so both are optional and
[`Task::effective_creator_id`] is the only correct way to ask.

description.description:
`None` is **the response did not say** — `GET /api/v1/tasks?omit=description` leaves the
key out and names it in `meta.omitted` — and `Some("")` is a description a person cleared.
They were one `""` until task ebe0966b (D55), which meant any write built from a cached row
erased text somebody had typed. [`Task::keeping_unsent`] fills an omitted one from the
cache; [`Task::description_text`] is what a reader that only draws or searches it wants.

dueDateTime.description:
The single source of truth for when the task is due. See [`super::date`] for what this
means when [`Task::is_all_day`] is set.

fields.description:
This task's GitHub project field VALUES, keyed by `ProjectField.id` (web AWTD-1208, spec
§9.4.3). No names and no types: those come once per project from
`GET /api/v1/projects/:id/fields`.

**`None` means "not asked", never "none".** The list route carries values only on
`?include=fields`, because a thousand tasks' worth is 42.2 KiB over an already tight
payload budget, while the task-detail route always carries them — and a task with no
values carries no key at all (web `lib/tasks/v1-task-fields.ts`). Those three cases are
indistinguishable here, so nothing may read an absent map as "this task has no field
values".

Which is why this is NOT where a pane reads them from:
`astrid_core::services::project_fields` caches the values under a key of their own, since
`store::upsert_task` replaces the whole encoded task and one list page fetched without
`?include=fields` would otherwise wipe what a detail fetch knew. What the key is modelled
FOR is the round trip — a value is only safe to cache and pass on once it survives a
decode and a re-encode, which is what task faa32e20 found it did not.

Values are `string | number` on the wire. They stay [`serde_json::Value`] because that is
already how a field value is represented where it is typed and validated
(`project_fields::accepts`), and two representations of one scalar is one too many.

identifier.description:
The human-readable id — `AST-142` (web task 12f54df4). Minted by the server for tasks on
a project; absent for a task on a project-less list, so a solo user never sees one.
Searchable as a direct hit.

isAllDay.description:
Defaults to **true**, matching the Swift memberwise init: a task created with a date and no
stated time is an all-day task.

nextOccurrenceId.description:
The occurrence that followed this one (web AWTD-1219). Only the single-task read and the
row beside a live event carry the key — an id, or `null` for "none" — and a list page
leaves it out. So absent (`None`) is "this response does not say", which
[`Task::keeping_unsent`] fills from the cache, and `Some(None)` is the server saying there
is no successor. Encodes back as it arrived, because the cache keeps the whole JSON.

originalTaskId.description: Copy lineage - the task this one was copied from. NOT the subtask relation.

parentTaskId.description:
Subtasks: the parent's id, `None` for a top-level task. A self-relation on the server,
nulled when the parent is deleted.

previousOccurrenceId.description:
The occurrence this one followed, on a list whose series spawns a new task each time
(web AWTD-1118). The link back; the way forward is the task that names this one here.

remote.description:
The GitHub issue or pull request a task on a GitHub board is (web AWTD-1222, spec §11.2).
Only a GitHub-backed task carries it; absent means classic.

statusRole.description:
Board status as a state ON the task: `ready` | `doing` | `waiting` | a project's custom
role. `None` means Inbox; Done is derived from `completed`, so neither is ever stored.

Tolerated as absent on purpose (task AWTD-562): a deployment older than the field simply
does not send it, and the board falls back to list membership. That fallback is what keeps
this build working against an unmigrated server.

syncState.description:
Where the server's write-back to the list's backend stands (web spec §11.2): `pending`
while a task made on a GitHub board is still being written there, `error` if that gave
up. Absent and `null` are both "settled" — it is a column on the task, so every response
carries it, and `null` is what a settled task and every classic list send.

admins.description:
Legacy denormalised arrays. Kept so the public-lists endpoint still decodes; **never**
consulted for a role — see [`crate::permissions`].

aiAgentsEnabled.description:
Accepts both the documented `string[]` and the object form the server once leaked. See the
module note.

backend.description:
Which backend holds this list (web AWTD-1256, spec §11.2): `"github_project"` for a GitHub
Projects board, `null` for a classic one. Ask through [`TaskList::is_github_backed`].

privacy.description: Absent from the thinner responses, so never assume a missing privacy means private.

projectId.description:
Project status board. A project holds both `listType: "regular"` (domain) lists and
`listType: "status"` (board column) lists. Inbox and Done are virtual columns derived from
task state and are never stored.

remote.description:
The GitHub Project this list mirrors (web AWTD-1222, spec §11.2), for the board's own chip
and its "open on GitHub". **`None` means there is no page**, which a classic list, an
iteration list and a board whose installation has gone all share — see [`ListRemote`].

showSubtasks.description: **`None` means SHOW.** See the module note and [`TaskList::shows_subtasks`].

supports.description:
What this list's backend can do (web AWTD-1190, spec §11.2). **`None` means classic**: a
server older than the field omits it. Ask through the methods, not the field.

TaskRemote.description: `task.remote`: where a task on a GitHub board lives on GitHub (web `lib/backends/task-remote.ts`).

url.description: The issue or pull request on GitHub. `None` for a draft, which has no page of its own.

defaultDueTime.description: `HH:MM`, the time of day a new all-day task defaults to when the user gives it a time.

email.description: Optional: the public-lists endpoint returns admins without their email addresses.

verified.description:
The account's own verification state, as `GET /users/me` merges it into the user (task
19fd9289): verified outright or through a sign-in provider, whether a change of address is
waiting, and what it is. Only ever present on the signed-in user; absent on everyone else,
and absent from a server older than the fields.

description:
The answer shapes that have a Rust type, gathered so one schema document holds them all.

A field per shape, named as the schema names it. It is never built or serialised — it exists so
`schemars` walks all of these in one pass and emits one set of `$defs`, with `Task` and `User`
written once rather than once per document.

**Adding a type here is the deliberate act.** A response shape that is not listed is not in the
schema, and a consumer's gate will say so about every field it carries — which is the right
failure, because the alternative is a gate that passes on shapes nobody described.
title: WireModels
